text: Does a sech^2 soliton IC for v, with u perturbed from v^2/2 by 0.2*v, produce a stable coherent soliton structure (peak >= 50% of initial amplitude, mass drift < 8%) at T=8 under the coupled Burgers-swept-KdV system?

ic: v0=2*sech^2(x+5), u0=0.5*v0^2+0.2*v0 (m=0.2*v0 perturbation from Gardner reduction; v_max=2.0, u_max=2.4)
method: Fourier pseudospectral + classical RK4 (all terms explicit, including v_xxx) + 2/3-rule dealiasing on all nonlinear products (zero modes |k_idx|>Nx/3=85)
bank_use_rationale: BKdV-S1 depth=3 confirms Fourier+2/3-rule+RK4 at dt=2e-4 is stable up to amp=3.0 and T=10 on exactly this domain (L=30, Nx=256); dispersive CFL with dealiased k_max=17.85 gives bound 4.97e-4 >> dt=2e-4. Rejecting no-dealiasing (CLOSED from BKdV-S1 single entry) and central-FD-Gibbs (CLOSED). BKdV-S6 bore-viscosity concern does NOT apply: our u0 is a smooth sech^2 profile, not a bore.

diagnostics.peak_fragmentation: severe - 36 dispersive peaks, dominant at x=-9.73
diagnostics.v_trajectory: monotone decay; crossed 1.0 threshold near T=3.5

rationale: v_max at T=8 is 0.679, well below the 1.0 threshold (50% of initial 2.0). Positive m=+0.2*v perturbation drives m_t = (v-1)(6vv_x+v_xxx) further from manifold monotonically, causing large u growth (7.5) which drains v via coupling -d_x(uv). Field is highly fragmented. Method (Fourier+RK4+2/3-dealias) is numerically sound (0% mass drift, no blowup); failure is physical.

Flip perturbation sign: u0 = 0.5*v^2 - 0.2*v (m0=-0.2*v). Negative m means source m_t=(v-1)(6vv_x+v_xxx)>0 initially pushes m toward 0, potentially limiting |m| growth and keeping u closer to v^2/2, thereby reducing the coupling that drains v. This is a single IC change; same Fourier+RK4+2/3-dealias method.

method: same as E1: Fourier pseudospectral + classical RK4 + 2/3-rule dealiasing
bank_use_rationale: Same BKdV-S1-confirmed method. IC change only: negative perturbation to test whether m_t source direction matters for v retention. No bank entry directly addresses this sign flip.

diagnostics.fine_grain_near_T8: v_max hits 1.154 at T=7.0, then falls to 0.710 by T=8.0 — oscillation period ~2 units, high point ~1 time unit before T=8

rationale: v_max=0.710 at T=8 (below 1.0 threshold). BUT v_max=1.154 at T=7.0 shows the system CAN sustain soliton amplitude above 1.0 — the oscillation peak is ~1 time unit before evaluation time. Negative perturbation slightly improved retention (35.5% vs 34% in E1) and reduced u growth (u_max=6.14 vs 7.52). The oscillation phase shift motivates E3.

Shift soliton x0 from -5 to -2 (3 units right = ~1.1 time-unit phase advance at soliton speed 2.67). This should place the oscillation peak at T~8 instead of T~7. Keep E2 IC form (negative perturbation, same method). Single change: x0 position.

ic: v0=2*sech^2(x+2) (x0 shifted from -5 to -2, +3 units right), u0=0.5*v0^2-0.2*v0 (same negative perturbation as E2)
method: same as E1/E2: Fourier pseudospectral + classical RK4 + 2/3-rule dealiasing, dt=2e-4
bank_use_rationale: F2 showed oscillation peak at T=7.0 (v_max=1.154). Phase shift of +3 spatial units intended to advance oscillation by ~1.12 time-units (3/2.67 at KdV soliton speed), placing peak at T~8.1. BKdV-S1 confirms method stability.

rationale: v_max=0.715 at T=8 — still below 1.0 threshold. Phase-shift strategy failed: the oscillation at x0=-2 peaks at T=7.2 with only 0.979 (below threshold), suggesting the oscillation is NOT a simple spatial phase-shift of the interaction dynamics. All three experiments consistently give ~35% retention at T=8. This appears to be a fundamental physical property: with u0~v^2/2, the coupling -d_x(uv) in the v equation continuously drains v amplitude as u grows from 2.4/1.6 to 5-7 over T=8. Mass conserved exactly; system bounded (u<7.5, v<2). Soliton partially survives as a coherent structure but with reduced amplitude.
